lesson_title: One Backpack, Followed All the Way: Manufacturing Cost Accounting
hook_text: What does ONE school backpack actually cost to make? Follow the rand and see.
clip_script: You are frying samoosas for the Saturday market — four hundred of them. What does ONE cost? Start sorting and you are doing cost accounting. Pastry, mince, spices — you can point at them folded inside the samoosa: direct materials. Your aunt frying all morning for a fee: direct labour. Together, prime cost — everything that touches the product. But the stand also burned gas, hired a table, wore out a borrowed fryer. None of that sits inside any one samoosa, yet without it nothing gets fried: that basket is overheads. And the posters you printed? Selling cost — a cost of the day, not of the samoosa. Keep it out, or the unit cost lies. Now scale up to a backpack factory: canvas issued to the floor, R488 000. Machinists' wages, R366 000. The overheads basket, R356 000. Out come 20 000 finished bags costing R1 200 000 — sixty rand a bag. That number is the factory's heartbeat. Price at ninety and you know, before selling one bag, what is left for the office, the deliveries and the profit. Watch sixty creep upward, and you know the floor is leaking before any statement says so. One rand, one path: shelves, floor, store, customer.
visual_style: A sizzling market stand morphing into a sewing floor, costs riding conveyor belts through four labelled stations, a glowing unit-cost heartbeat monitor; warm Limpopo workshop palette with canvas and chalk textures.
pacing: Playful samoosa sort, then a driving conveyor sequence to the heartbeat reveal.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and walk the rand's whole path yourself.
